cards.text: This is a letter from Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and a brother of James. He writes to those who are called, loved by God the Father, and kept in Jesus Christ. Friend, if my mail ever came addressed like that, I'd frame the envelope and hang it over the oven.
Then he wishes them mercy, peace, and love, not just handed out but MULTIPLIED. That's the difference between one cookie and a full tray, friend.
Jude admits he'd made every effort to write to them about the salvation they all share. But he felt he had to write and urge them to do something else.

cards.question: Instead of writing about their shared salvation, Jude urges them to ___ earnestly for the faith.
Jude says this faith was entrusted to the saints once for all. What does that tell you about it?

answers.text: It changes with every new leader

cards.text: Here's why: certain men have crept in among them unnoticed, ungodly ones who were designated long ago for condemnation. Like ants in the cookie box, nobody EVER sees the first one walk in.

cards.question: Jude calls the men who crept in ungodly ones. What do they turn the grace of our God into?
The men who crept in still honor Jesus Christ as their only Master and Lord.

cards.text: Jude says they're fully aware of all this, but he's going to remind them anyway, starting with the people Jesus delivered out of the land of Egypt. That's me and my oven timer, friend: I KNOW, and I still need the beep.

cards.question: Jude says that after Jesus delivered His people out of Egypt, He let those who did not believe go unpunished.

cards.text: Next reminder: the angels who did not stay within their own domain but abandoned their proper dwelling. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer with a takeout menu for a blanket, and these angels walked away from a PROPER DWELLING.

cards.question: Those angels are bound for judgment on that great day. Where are they being kept until then?

answers.text: In a pit out in the wilderness
In the lions' den in Babylon

cards.text: Then Jude points to Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them. They indulged in sexual immorality and pursued strange flesh.

cards.question: Jude says Sodom and Gomorrah are on display as an ___ of those who sustain the punishment of eternal fire.

cards.text: Now Jude swings back to the men who crept in and calls them dreamers. In the same way, they defile their bodies, reject authority, and slander glorious beings.
Now compare that to Michael, the archangel, who once got into a dispute with the devil himself. The DEVIL, friend, the one guy who's got every hard word in the world coming to him.

cards.question: What were Michael the archangel and the devil disputing over?
Even with the devil, Michael did not presume to bring a slanderous charge against him. So what does Michael say?
Michael held back his words. Jude says the men who crept in only slander what they understand well.

cards.text: They slander what they do not understand. And like irrational animals, they will be destroyed by the things they do instinctively.
Jude isn't finished with these men. "Woe to them!" he says, and he lines them up with three men from long ago.
Cain, Adam's son who killed his brother Abel (Gen 4:1, 8), and Korah, who rose up against Moses (Num 16:1-3). And Balaam, a prophet hired to curse Israel (Deut 23:4).

cards.question: Jude says these men have rushed for profit into the error of ___.

cards.text: Now the pictures start: these men are hidden reefs in their love feasts, shamelessly feasting with them but shepherding only themselves. That's the guy who volunteers to guard the cookie table, and somehow the table keeps getting LIGHTER.

cards.question: A hidden reef sits just under the surface of the water. What does that picture say about these men at the love feasts?

answers.text: They are dangerous and hard to see
They keep the church safe from storms
They slowly wear away over time

cards.text: Next picture: they're clouds without water, carried along by the wind. You know that cookie box you shake and it RATTLES, so you get all excited, and you open it, and it's CRUMBS.

cards.question: Jude's picture of clouds without water says these men bring real refreshment to the church.

cards.text: They're fruitless trees in autumn, twice dead after being uprooted, and wild waves of the sea, foaming up their own shame. Then Jude calls them wandering stars.

cards.question: Jude calls these men wandering stars. What has been reserved for them forever?

cards.text: Then Jude brings in Enoch, the seventh from Adam, who prophesied about these men. Enoch lived way back in Genesis, friend, and he was ALREADY talking about these guys (Gen 5:18-24).

cards.question: In Enoch's prophecy, who is coming with myriads of His holy ones?
Enoch says the Lord will convict the ungodly of their wicked acts, but not of the harsh words they spoke against Him.

cards.text: Jude piles it on: these men are discontented grumblers, following after their own lusts, and their mouths spew arrogance. Grumbling AND bragging at the same time? Friend, that takes stamina.

cards.question: And these grumblers ___ others for their own advantage.

cards.text: Then Jude turns back to his readers, the beloved, and tells them to remember what the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ foretold. Basically, friend: you were WARNED about these guys.

cards.question: What did the apostles say there would be in the last times?

answers.text: Scoffers following their own ungodly desires
A great famine across the land

cards.question: Jude says these scoffers are the ones who bring believers together.

cards.text: So what do the beloved do? Jude hands them a recipe: build yourselves up in your most holy faith, and pray in the Holy Spirit.

cards.question: As they build themselves up and pray, Jude tells them to keep themselves in the ___ of God.
While they keep themselves in God's love, what does Jude say they are waiting for?

answers.text: The mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ
A new letter from the apostles
The temple to be built again

cards.text: Then Jude points them outward, toward other people. And not everybody gets the same thing from them.

cards.question: What does Jude tell them to have on those who doubt?
Others, Jude says, they should save by snatching them from the ___.

cards.text: And to still others, they show mercy tempered with fear, hating even the clothing stained by the flesh.
Jude doesn't end on a warning, he ends with praise to the One who is able to keep them from stumbling. Friend, I hop around this bakery on a gold base all day, so believe me, I APPRECIATE that.

cards.question: Jude says God is able to present them in His glorious presence. How?
Jude says glory, majesty, dominion, and authority belong to the only God our Savior before all time, now, and for all eternity.

cards.text: All of it through Jesus Christ our Lord, and Jude seals it with one word: Amen. Friend, THAT is how you close a box.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks for 'contend', but card 3 only says Jude wants to 'urge them to do something else'. Nothing told so far points to 'contend' over 'search' or 'wait'. The reason (men crept in) isn't told until card 6. This makes the baker guess wording they haven't seen.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Cain, Korah and Balaam are introduced, but Jude's own words about Cain and Korah ('traveled the path of Cain', 'perished in Korah's rebellion') are never told on any card. Only the Balaam line is covered (card 3), so the baker misses two-thirds of verse 11.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Balaam is called 'a prophet' with the reference Deut 23:4, but that verse doesn't call him a prophet. It only says he was hired to curse Israel. The stated fact doesn't match its reference.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: 'Now the pictures start' isn't true. Jude already used a picture in verse 10 ('like irrational animals'), which was told on stop 1 card 20.

rule.text: Noticing. What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The joke about the rattling cookie box that turns out to be crumbs spells out what 'clouds without water' means (empty, all promise). That gives away the answer to the true or false on card 7 (no real refreshment).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card carries three separate images: fruitless trees, wild waves, and wandering stars.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The reference Gen 5:18-24 is attached to 'he was ALREADY talking about these guys'. This suggests Genesis records Enoch's prophecy, but Genesis 5 says nothing about it. Only Jude 1:14 does.

rule.text: Connecting passages. When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'Jude piles it on…', 'Grumbling AND bragging at the same time?', 'Friend, that takes stamina.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
